attempted_claim: Let A be a unital simple separable nuclear Q-stable stably finite C*-algebra, where Q is the universal UHF algebra, and suppose every tracial state on A is quasidiagonal. Must A have generalized tracial rank at most one? Equivalently, for every finite F contained in A, every epsilon greater than zero, and every nonzero positive element a in A, must there exist a nonzero projection p in A and an Elliott-Thomsen one-dimensional NCCW subalgebra C contained in pAp with unit p such that ||xp-px|| is less than epsilon and dist(pxp,C) is less than epsilon for every x in F, and 1-p is Cuntz subequivalent to a?
decisive_failure: The lane established that the Q-stable target is exactly the UCT-free Elliott-Gong-Lin-Niu statement via the CETWW finite-nuclear-dimension theorem, but could resolve neither direction: proof requires removing UCT from EGLN and disproof requires a nuclear non-UCT algebra, both tantamount to progress on the open UCT problem and beyond bounded effort. No fallback was available and no original increment was produced.
